To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we establish explicit convergence rates of the ground state of the Thomas--Ferni--von Weisz\"acker model from the Yukawa setting to the Coulomb setting.

we have established uniform convergence, with an explicit rate, of solutions to the Thomas-- Fermi--von Weitzs\"acker (TWF) Yukawa model, with general condensed nuclei, to solutions of the TWF Coulomb model, and have established convergence of forces from one model to the other.
the ground state solution to the TFW Yukawa model converges to the ground state solution of the TFS model as $\alpha\to\infty$, where $\alpha$ is the strength of the Yukawa interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the ground state of a system of $N$ fermions interacting through the Yukawa potential.
the mathematical study of the TFW model in the Yukawa setting, which is a physically relevant model for the study of the electronic structure of atoms and molecules.
the mathematical study of the TFW model with Yukawa interaction, a model which was introduced by Lieb (1981) to study the stability of matter for a class of nuclear configurations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Yukawa model is a good approximation for the Coulomb model, and that the rate of convergence is explicit and uniform in the nuclear configuration.
the Coulomb and Yukawa TFW models are equivalent for the ground state, in the sense that their respective solutions are close in the sense of a uniform norm.

, for the TFW model, we can now prove that the Yukawa interaction is an excellent approximation of the Coulomb interaction in terms of the ground state energy, the ground state density, and the ground state forces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the convergence rate of the solution from the Yukawa model to that of the Coulomb model is of order $1/\alpha$, where $\alpha$ is the screening parameter of the Yukawa interaction.
we establish the existence of the TFW Yukawa ground state for general nuclear configurations and we show the existence of the limit as the coupling constant tends to infinity.

we have established a rigorous mathematical framework for the use of Yukawa potentials in electronic structure calculations, and that this framework is applicable to the most general condensed matter configurations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the convergence of ground states from Yukawa to the corresponding Coulomb models holds for general condensed nuclear configuration and with explicit rate.

, in the context of the TFW model, the convergence of ground state energies and forces from the Yukawian to the Coulombian setting can be rigorously justified, and the convergence rate can be estimated explicitly.
